display.purpose: The large sign on the login screen only.

numeral.purpose: One big figure per plate: the briefing temperature, the money balance.

headline.purpose: Arabic line of every screen sign; the briefing greeting.

title.purpose: Section headings, poll questions, free-together windows.

time.purpose: Route-stop times, prayer names on stops, calendar times.

label.purpose: Meta lines, tabs, chips, notices, toasts.

sign-caption.purpose: The English line beneath the Arabic on a sign.

micro.purpose: Units and companions to a larger figure: am/pm, hour labels, rain chance, badges.

narrative.northStar: Street Signs on a Night Street
narrative.overview:
Abdo is a Cairene roommate, so his app is dressed in the most Cairene object there is: the blue enamel street sign, with white lettering and a white ring set in from the edge. The signs hang on a navy night. Everything Abdo says is a plate: each screen's title, his chat bubbles, the morning briefing, the money balance. Everything else sits quietly on the navy (rows, hairlines, soft secondary text), so the plates carry the screen.

On top of the blue and white there is one signal colour: gold, for whatever is happening now or needs you next. That covers the "now" tick on the day's route line, the next prayer, the active tab, the needs-you chips, the hold-to-talk mic and the focus ring. The screens are dense and built for a quick glance on a phone held in one hand: a single column, rows at least 44 to 52px tall, and times and numbers set in the sign face with tabular figures so they line up like a timetable.

The app speaks two languages throughout. Titles read Arabic first in large type, with English beneath at caption size, the way a bilingual street sign does. Every line of mixed text reads in its own direction. The app is dark only for now.
keyCharacteristics: Enamel-blue plates with an inset white ring mark Abdo's own voice; nothing else gets a plate.
One navy night ground with tonal surfaces and hairlines; no drop-shadow elevation.
Gold signals now, next and act; it is never decoration.
Two faces: Alexandria for signs, headings, times and numbers; IBM Plex Sans Arabic for running text.
Arabic-first bilingual titles; `unicode-bidi: plaintext` on every mixed line.
Today is a transit route: a 4px enamel-blue line with ring stops, square bus stops, and a terminus bar.

rules.name: The Enamel Voice Rule
rules.body: A plate (enamel blue, white ring, white lettering) means Abdo is speaking or a screen is naming itself: screen titles, his chat bubbles, the briefing, the money balance. Ordinary rows, lists and forms never sit on a plate.

rules.name: The Gold Means Now Rule
rules.body: Gold marks only what is current, next, active or waiting on you. If a gold element doesn't answer "what's happening now, or what should I do?", it shouldn't be gold.

rules.name: The Arabic Leads Rule
rules.body: Every screen title is a sign: the Arabic name large on top, the English name beneath at caption size. Arabic is never the smaller line.

rules.name: The Two Faces Rule
rules.body: Alexandria for anything a sign would show (names, headings, times, numbers); Plex Sans Arabic for sentences. Don't add a third family.

rules.name: The Timetable Figures Rule
rules.body: Times, temperatures, amounts and counts use tabular figures (`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`), so columns of times line up like a schedule.

rules.name: The Own-Direction Rule
rules.body: Every text surface that can mix scripts uses `unicode-bidi: plaintext`. In lists, also pin `text-align: left`, so Arabic rows don't flush right. Chat bubbles keep `dir="auto"` alignment on purpose.

rules.name: The Route Grammar
rules.body: Today lays out time as a transit line. The list is indented 30px, and a 4px enamel-blue line runs down the left with rounded caps. Each stop is a three-column grid: a 62px time, then the content, then an optional action. Each stop marker is a 14px ring centred on the line. The gold "now" tick (18 by 4px) crosses the line at the current moment, and a 16px terminus bar closes the line under the last stop.

rules.name: The Ring, Not Shadow Rule
rules.body: Plates get their presence from the inset white ring and the blue. Cards, rows and plates never get drop shadows.

dos: Do give each screen exactly one street-sign title, Arabic on top and English beneath, centred in the fixed header.
Do put Abdo's own words (his briefing, his chat bubbles, the balance he keeps) on an enamel plate with the inset white ring.
Do keep gold for now, next, active and needs-you. Gold fills are only for the mic and the "mark paid" action, with Blue-Black Ink text on them.
Do set times, temperatures and amounts in Alexandria with tabular figures.
Do use `unicode-bidi: plaintext` on every line that can mix scripts, and `text-align: left` in lists.
Do keep tap targets at least 44px, and use logical properties (`inset-inline-start`, `border-end-start-radius`) so the layout mirrors cleanly in right-to-left text.
Do respect `prefers-reduced-motion`: the now-tick draw, the chevron turn, the switch slide and the recording pulse all turn off.
donts: Don't put drop shadows on plates, cards or rows. Depth is the ring and the navy tones.
Don't put ordinary lists, forms or settings on a plate. A plate means Abdo or a screen title.
Don't use gold as decoration, or in large fills beyond the mic and the settle-up action.
Don't make English the larger or leading line in a title.
Don't add a third typeface, an icon font, or emoji standing in for icons.
Don't add a light theme or light surfaces without a deliberate system change. The world is a night street.
Don't let an Arabic row flush right inside a list.
